newsitem.title: INDONESIA: New chief calls on Indonesian army to protect poll.
newsitem.headline: New chief calls on Indonesian army to protect poll.

text.p: Indonesia's new army chief of staff General Wiranto has said in his first public statement since assuming his post that the military stood ready to counter any attempt to disrupt next year's presidential elections.

"ABRI (the armed forces) is committed to safeguarding and making the 1998 MPR general session a success because the meeting will decide who will be the national leader," Wiranto was quoted as saying by the Antara news agency on Wednesday.

Wiranto, appointed last week and regarded as a potential successor to General Feisal Tanjung as the armed forces chief, said the armed forces would remain on high alert to face what he described as certain groups attempting to make radical changes.
Tanjung said last week the military had identified people who it said attempted to foil the May 29 general elections to the 500-member House of Representatives (DPR).

The People's Consultative Assembly, made up of the newly elected DPR members and 500 government appointees, will meet in Jakarta in March to approve the guidelines for state policy and elect the president and vice president.
President Suharto, in power for almost 30 years, is widely expected to be elected unopposed for another five-year term.

The military has blamed the unrecognised People's Democratic Party and other unnamed "third parties" for sparking the widespread rioting, mostly on the main island of Java, which marred the 27-day campaign for the general elections.
Authorities say more than 300 people died during the campaign, mostly in traffic accidents, while 124 died in a shopping centre fire during a riot in South Kalimantan.

The ruling Golkar party swept the national poll with over 74 percent of the vote. The Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) won just under 23 percent and the badly-split Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) won only three percent.
